indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.1.1.1 Understand the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicator.objective: Know the life processes of living things (growth, sensitivity to the environment, respiration and excretion)

skills.description: Identify growth, sensitivity, respiration and excretion as life processes of living things.
Describe growth as an increase in size over time (e.g. a seedling becoming a mature plant).
Describe sensitivity as the ability of living things to respond to changes in their environment (e.g. mimosa plant closing when touched).
Describe respiration as the process of breathing in and out to get energy.
Describe excretion as the removal of waste products from the body.
Explain simply why each life process is important for living things.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Excretion is the same as eating.
Growth means only getting taller (not all living things grow the same way).
Respiration and breathing are exactly the same thing.

questions.stem: Which of these is a life process of living things?
hints: Think about what all living things do.
It is one of the four life processes you learned.
questions.explanation: Growth is a life process. The four life processes in this lesson are growth, sensitivity, respiration and excretion.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the four life processes of living things?
hints: Think about the four processes you learned.
Dancing is an activity, not a life process.
questions.explanation: The four life processes are growth, sensitivity, respiration and excretion. Dancing is not a life process.
questions.misconception: Any activity is a life process.

questions.stem: What does growth mean in living things?
hints: Think about a seed becoming a plant.
Growth means getting bigger.
questions.explanation: Growth means increasing in size over time. A seedling grows into a mature plant.

questions.stem: What is sensitivity in living things?
options: The ability to respond to changes in the environment
hints: Think about the mimosa plant closing when touched.
It is about responding to changes.
questions.explanation: Sensitivity is the ability of living things to respond to changes in their environment.

questions.stem: What is respiration?
options: The process of breathing in and out to get energy
hints: You do this all the time without thinking.
It involves breathing.
questions.explanation: Respiration is the process of breathing in and out to get energy from food.
questions.misconception: Respiration and breathing are exactly the same thing.

questions.stem: Ama plants a bean seed. After two weeks, the plant is taller and has more leaves. Which life process is this?
hints: The plant is getting bigger.
It is increasing in size.
questions.explanation: The plant is growing. Growth is the increase in size over time.

questions.stem: When you touch the leaves of a mimosa plant, they fold up. What life process is the plant showing?
hints: The plant is responding to touch.
It is reacting to a change.
questions.explanation: The mimosa plant is responding to touch. This is sensitivity — responding to changes in the environment.

questions.stem: A pupil breathes in and out quickly after running. Which life process is this?
hints: The pupil is breathing.
Breathing is part of respiration.
questions.explanation: The pupil is respiring. Respiration is breathing in and out to get energy.
questions.misconception: Respiration only happens when we sleep.

questions.stem: What is excretion?
options: The process of removing waste products from the body
The process of responding to touch
hints: Think about what the body removes as waste.
It is not eating.
questions.explanation: Excretion is the removal of waste products from the body, such as urine and sweat.
questions.misconception: Excretion is the same as eating.

questions.stem: Why is respiration important for living things?
options: It gives them energy to live and work
It helps them respond to touch
hints: What does breathing give the body?
It provides energy.
questions.explanation: Respiration gives living things energy to live, grow and work.
questions.misconception: Respiration is only for making noise.

questions.stem: What is growth in living things?
hints: Think about a seed becoming a plant.
It means increasing in size.
questions.explanation: Growth is the increase in size of a living thing over time.

questions.stem: What is respiration?
answer: breathing in and out to get energy
the process of breathing to get energy
hints: You do it all the time.
It gives you energy.
questions.explanation: Respiration is the process of breathing in and out to get energy from food.
questions.misconception: Respiration and breathing are not related.

questions.stem: A pupil touches a snail and it quickly pulls back into its shell. What does this show?
hints: The snail is responding to touch.
It is reacting to a change.
questions.explanation: The snail is responding to touch by pulling back. This is sensitivity.

questions.stem: Why is excretion important for living things?
options: It removes waste products that can harm the body
It helps them respond to touch
hints: What happens if waste stays in the body?
It can harm the body.
questions.explanation: Excretion removes waste products that would harm the body if they stayed inside.

questions.stem: A pupil observes a seedling and a mature plant of the same kind. Which difference shows growth?
options: The mature plant is taller and has more leaves
The mature plant is a different colour
The mature plant is in a different pot
The mature plant has a different smell
hints: Growth means getting bigger.
What happens to size over time?
questions.explanation: The mature plant is taller and has more leaves, showing it has grown.

questions.stem: Give an example of a plant showing sensitivity.
answer: the mimosa plant folds its leaves when touched
hints: Think about a plant that moves when touched.
It is called the mimosa.
questions.explanation: The mimosa plant folds its leaves when touched. This is an example of sensitivity in plants.

questions.stem: Why is sensitivity important for living things?
answer: it helps them respond to danger and changes in their environment
it helps them react to changes around them
hints: Think about responding to danger.
It helps them react to the environment.
questions.explanation: Sensitivity helps living things respond to changes and danger in their environment, helping them survive.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of excretion in humans?
hints: The body removes waste.
Urine is a waste product.
questions.explanation: Passing out urine is an example of excretion. The body removes waste products.
questions.misconception: Excretion is the same as eating.

questions.stem: Explain how a seedling shows growth over time.
answer: it gets taller and develops more leaves as it grows
the seedling increases in size and grows more leaves
it grows bigger and taller over time
hints: What happens to size?
What happens to the number of leaves?
questions.explanation: A seedling shows growth by getting taller and developing more leaves over time.

questions.stem: Explain why living things need respiration.
answer: respiration gives the body energy to live and work
it provides energy for life processes
hints: What does breathing give the body?
It provides energy.
questions.explanation: Living things need respiration to get energy from food. This energy is used for growth, movement and other life processes.
questions.misconception: Respiration is not needed for energy.

questions.stem: A pupil lists four life processes: growth, sensitivity, respiration and excretion. Which statement about these processes is correct?
options: Only animals show all four processes
Only humans show all four processes
Plants show only growth and respiration
hints: Do plants grow?
Do plants respond to touch?
Do plants breathe?
questions.explanation: Plants show all four life processes: growth, sensitivity, respiration and excretion. They grow, respond to touch, respire and excrete waste.
